thinkingMessage.text:
Two SignIn handlers exist in the repository.

`APIV1Service.SignIn` in `auth_service.go` is the primary backend handler. `ConnectServiceHandler.SignIn` in `connect_services.go` appears to be a wrapper. I am reading both files to confirm the exact call chain.
Searching connect_services.go for the Connect SignIn handler.

The repository structure is now clear.

The SignIn RPC is defined in `proto/api/v1/auth_service.proto`. The Connect protocol wrapper is `ConnectServiceHandler.SignIn` in `connect_services.go`. The actual business logic is implemented by `APIV1Service.SignIn` in `auth_service.go`.

The Connect wrapper delegates directly to `APIV1Service.SignIn` in `auth_service.go`. The gRPC gateway registers this same method via `RegisterAuthServiceHandlerServer`. The exact answer is `APIV1Service.SignIn` at `server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go`.

Two RPC entry points were identified.

`APIV1Service.SignIn` in `auth_service.go` is the actual backend implementation. `ConnectServiceHandler.SignIn` in `connect_services.go` is merely a thin wrapper delegating to it.

The SignIn RPC is handled by `APIV1Service.SignIn` in `server/router/api/v1/auth_service.go`.

The gRPC-Gateway registers this handler directly. Connect routes through `ConnectServiceHandler.SignIn`, which delegates to `APIV1Service.SignIn`. The proto RPC is `AuthService.SignIn`, but the Go implementation type is `APIV1Service`.
